title: J. E. H. Duckworth MC LDS RCS Eng (1897–1957) and the London Group Circular: politics, polemics and prophecies
html: J. E. H. Duckworth was a London-based dental practitioner who, following decorated action in the First World War and a period living in South Africa, set up practice in North London in the 1930s. From there, during the Second World War, he became heavily involved in dental politics through the Group Movement, which evolved from the committees of local practitioners set up to support absent mobilised dentists and their practices. The Movement became a force for unity in the profession, bringing together the three representative organisations of the time but, largely through Duckworth and his monthly publication of a circular newsletter, became one of the voices opposed to the introduction of a national dental service. This paper presents a portrait of the polymath J. E. H. Duckworth, and the arguments presented against the introduction of a dental National Health Service, seen largely through his writings in the London Dental Circular.
